newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI confirms Johnson sale, mulls options.
newsitem.headline: JCI confirms Johnson sale, mulls options.

text.p: South African mining house JCI Ltd on Friday confirmed its sale of a stake in Britain's Johnson Matthey Plc, but said it had not yet decided what to do with the cash.
JCI is exploring ways to fund a buy of 26.8 percent of British conglomerate Lonrho Plc for some 2.5 billion rand.
"(The Johnson Matthey cash) could be used in that respect, but that is a decision that doesn't have to be taken yet," a JCI spokesman told Reuters.
He added an official statement on the sale would be made later on Friday.
JCI shares were down 15 cents to 30.10 rand at 1045 GMT.

Analysts had been expecting the Johnson Matthey sale and are speculating on other options such as the sale or merger of its unlisted Tavistock coal division with Lonrho and the disposal of non-core assets such as a 9.8 percent stake in Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd.
Earlier on Friday Johnson Matthey said JCI had sold its 18.9 million share stake through investment bank SBC Warburg at 560p per share.
Johnson Matthey chief executive Gordon Thorburn told Reuters he understood the stock had been placed with a number of institutional investors.
